author: Zephyr I
title: Width ablation on bottleneck-dilated d=5: 32/64 vs 48/96 (single-step LN-ConvLSTM)
abstract: Evaluate modest width scaling with compute-efficient bottleneck-dilated residuals: compare CNN widths 32/64 vs 48/96 on the non-FE d=5 single-step LN-ConvLSTM baseline under default PG; BASE_SEED=42.

original_submission.content:
import sys
sys.path.append('storage/zephyr')
from networks.cnn_convlstm_layernorm_single_step_dilated_bottleneck import DilatedBottleneckSotaNet
from ray import tune

BASE_SEED = 42

def _define_hyperparameters():
    return {
        'learning_rate': tune.choice([4e-4]),
        'entropy_coef': tune.choice([0.01]),
        'value_loss_coef': tune.choice([0.5]),
        'cnn_features_1': tune.choice([32, 48]),
        'cnn_features_2': tune.choice([64, 96]),
        'conv_lstm_features': tune.choice([64]),
        'bottleneck_ratio': tune.choice([0.5]),
        'use_silu': tune.choice([False]),
    }

def create_network(hparams):
    return DilatedBottleneckSotaNet(
        cnn_features_1=int(hparams['cnn_features_1']),
        cnn_features_2=int(hparams['cnn_features_2']),
        conv_lstm_features=64,
        dilation=5,
        bottleneck_ratio=0.5,
        use_silu=False,
    )
